findings.title: Attacker-controlled flag name crashes parser via inherited property on aliases object
findings.impact: `aliases` is a plain `{}`. For a flag such as `--constructor x`, `--__proto__ x`, `--toString x` or `--valueOf x`, `aliases[key]` resolves to an inherited, truthy Object.prototype member. The new `aliasIsBoolean` then calls `.some` on it. That member is not an array, so this throws a TypeError. Any program that parses untrusted argv can be made to crash, which is a denial of service. Before this change such input did not throw at this point.
findings.recommendation: Create `aliases` with `Object.create(null)`, or guard with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(aliases, key)`. Apply the same guard in `argDefined` and in the new condition at line 119. Also check `Array.isArray` inside `aliasIsBoolean`.
